One analysis for every comparison of fluconazole with another condition. It replaces
`Fig4.effect-size-comparison-replicates.Rmd`, `Fig4.effect-size-comparison-best-replicates.Rmd`
and `Fig4.effect-size-comparison-flu-doses-vs-baselines.Rmd`.

**Direction (the same everywhere in this file).** Every comparison starts from the
fluconazole eQTLs: each variant-gene pair that is significant in fluconazole_16ug (16 ug/ml) or
fluconazole_8ug (8 ug/ml) is looked up in another condition (e.g. YPD.1) among *all tested*
variants of the same gene (`first_assoc` files). The pair does not need to be significant in that
condition. The question is always "are fluconazole eQTLs seen in the other condition, and with the
same effect?". A comparison is named after the condition the eQTLs come from and the condition they
are looked up in, e.g. "fluconazole_16ug eQTLs in YPD.1"; in every scatter plot the condition looked
up in is on x and fluconazole on y.

| Significant eQTLs of | Looked up in |
|---|---|
| fluconazole_16ug, fluconazole_8ug (two drug doses, not replicates) | YPD.1, YPD.2, synthetic complete (sc2glu.2), YPD (integrated YPD.1 + YPD.2), synthetic complete (integrated sc2glu.1 + sc2glu.2) |
| Galactose (scgal.1), Section 5 | the same five conditions, plus fluconazole_16ug and fluconazole_8ug |
| YPD.1 and YPD.2, Section 6 (replicate reference) | the other YPD replicate |

Section 5 repeats Sections 2-4 with the galactose eQTLs in place of the fluconazole eQTLs
(galactose eQTLs looked up in each of the other conditions; that condition on x, galactose on y).
Its outputs go to `../results/flu_eQTLs_in_baselines/galactose/`. Section 6 runs the same comparison
between the two YPD replicates (expected agreement from replication alone), Section 7 puts
all comparisons in one table, and Section 8 is the summary table.

All eight datasets use the YPD.1 genotype files, FaST-LMM settings and pseudobulk steps.

# 1. Datasets and inputs

```{r config}
ROOT <- "/projects/rps/cgsb/gresham/Akriti/wildyeast1/common_analysis_for_all"
OUTPUT_DIR <- "../results/flu_eQTLs_in_baselines"
dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
N_CORES <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "8"))
N_PERMS <- 5000
set.seed(42)

SNP_DIR   <- "results_SNPs_96_MAF15_from_969_strains_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5"
INDEL_DIR <- "results_Indels_96_MAF15_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5"
CNV_DIR   <- "results_CNVs_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_no_chr17"   # CNV GWAS re-run without chr17
SV_DIR    <- "results_SVs_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files"

make_cond <- function(res, tag, indel_dir = INDEL_DIR,
                      indel_file = paste0("all_signif_Indels_", tag, "_96_MAF15_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt")) {
  res <- file.path(ROOT, res)
  list(signif = c(
         SNPs   = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_SNPs_", tag, "_96_MAF15_from_969_strains_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt")),
         InDels = file.path(res, indel_file),
         SVs    = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_SVs_", tag, "_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_with_threshold.txt")),
         CNVs   = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_CNV_", tag, "_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_no_chr17_with_threshold.txt"))),
       dirs = c(SNPs = file.path(res, SNP_DIR), InDels = file.path(res, indel_dir),
                SVs = file.path(res, SV_DIR), CNVs = file.path(res, CNV_DIR)))
}

CONDS <- list(
  Flu.1             = make_cond("Flu.1/fastlmm/results", "Flu.1"),
  Flu.2             = make_cond("Flu.2/fastlmm/results", "Flu.2"),
  YPD.1             = make_cond("YPD.1/fastlmm/results", "YPD.1",   # YPD.1's InDel run: other folder, same indels.96samples
                                indel_dir  = "results_Indels_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5",
                                indel_file = "all_signif_Indels_YPD.1_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt"),
  YPD.2             = make_cond("YPD.2/fastlmm/results", "YPD.2"),
  sc2glu.2          = make_cond("sc2glu.2/fastlmm_sc2.glu.2_only/results", "sc2glu.2_only"),
  YPD_integrated    = make_cond("merged_YPD/fastlmm/results", "merged_YPD"),
  sc2glu_integrated = make_cond("sc2glu.2/fastlmm/results", "sc2glu.2"),
  scgal.1           = make_cond("scgal.1/fastlmm/results", "scgal.1"))

FLU   <- c(Flu.1 = "fluconazole_16ug", Flu.2 = "fluconazole_8ug")   # 16 ug/ml, 8 ug/ml
BASE  <- c(YPD.1 = "YPD.1", YPD.2 = "YPD.2", sc2glu.2 = "synthetic complete",
           YPD_integrated = "YPD (integrated)", sc2glu_integrated = "synthetic complete (integrated)")
VARIANTS <- c("SNPs", "InDels", "SVs", "CNVs")

# one row per comparison (eQTL condition x condition looked up in); `flu` / `flu_lab` hold the query dataset (fluconazole
# here, galactose in Section 5), `short` = its short label;
# `bases` = the datasets the query is looked up in (BASE, plus both doses for galactose)
# file-name tags: the two fluconazole datasets are doses, not replicates
dose_tag <- function(x) dplyr::recode(x, Flu.1 = "Flu_16ug", Flu.2 = "Flu_8ug")
make_comp <- function(query, short, bases = BASE) expand_grid(flu = names(query), base = names(bases)) %>%
  mutate(flu_lab = query[flu], base_lab = bases[base], short = short[flu],
         comparison = paste0(short, " eQTLs in ", base_lab),
         file_tag = gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", paste0(dose_tag(flu), "_in_", dose_tag(base))))
COMP <- make_comp(FLU, FLU)
COMP_LEVELS <- COMP$comparison
BASE_COLS <- c("YPD.1" = "#81C784", "YPD.2" = "#2E7D32", "synthetic complete" = "#E65100",
               "YPD (integrated)" = "#1565C0", "synthetic complete (integrated)" = "#FFB74D",
               "fluconazole_16ug" = "#BA68C8", "fluconazole_8ug" = "#6A1B9A")

missing <- c(unlist(lapply(CONDS, `[[`, "signif")), unlist(lapply(CONDS, `[[`, "dirs")))
missing <- missing[!file.exists(missing)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Missing inputs:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))
COMP %>% select(comparison, flu_lab, base_lab)
```

```{r load-signif}
# significant eQTLs, one row per variant-gene pair and variant type
signif <- lapply(CONDS, function(cfg) bind_rows(lapply(VARIANTS, function(vt)
  fread(cfg$signif[[vt]], sep = "\t", quote = "", data.table = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(Gene = Source_Phenotype, SNP, Variant_Type = vt, Beta = SnpWeight, P = PValue))) %>%
  distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type, .keep_all = TRUE))

signif_counts <- bind_rows(lapply(names(signif), function(k)
  signif[[k]] %>% count(Variant_Type) %>% mutate(dataset = k))) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Variant_Type, values_from = n) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(any_of(VARIANTS))), genes_with_sig_eQTL = sapply(signif[dataset], function(d) n_distinct(d$Gene)))
knitr::kable(signif_counts, caption = "Significant eQTLs (variant-gene pairs) and genes with a significant eQTL per dataset")
```

# 2. Look up the fluconazole eQTLs in the other conditions

For each other condition and gene, that condition's `first_assoc` file is read once and the
variants significant in fluconazole_16ug or fluconazole_8ug for that gene are kept (one table per condition, shared by
both doses: `sapply(lookups, nrow)` counts the pairs of *either* dose found there). Cached to
`lookup_<condition>.rds`. Each comparison then uses only its own dose's eQTLs (`query_in_base()`).
# names(FLU) is both Flu.1 and Flu.2, so flu_pairs is the combined list of gene-variant pairs from both doses
so output is flu.1 +flu.2
```{r lookup}
read_first_assoc <- function(path, snps) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  d <- tryCatch(fread(path, sep = "\t", select = c("SNP", "SnpWeight", "PValue"), showProgress = FALSE),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(d)) NULL else d[SNP %in% snps]
}
flu_pairs <- bind_rows(signif[names(FLU)]) %>% distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type)

build_lookup <- function(b, pairs = flu_pairs, out_dir = OUTPUT_DIR) {
  cache <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("lookup_", b, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(cache)) return(readRDS(cache))
  jobs <- pairs %>% group_by(Variant_Type, Gene) %>% summarise(snps = list(SNP), .groups = "drop")
  res <- mclapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(i) {
    vt <- jobs$Variant_Type[i]; g <- jobs$Gene[i]
    d <- read_first_assoc(file.path(CONDS[[b]]$dirs[[vt]], g, paste0(g, ".first_assoc.txt")), jobs$snps[[i]])
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
    d[, `:=`(Gene = g, Variant_Type = vt)]
  }, mc.cores = N_CORES)
  lk <- rbindlist(res) %>% as.data.frame() %>% distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type, .keep_all = TRUE)
  saveRDS(lk, cache)
  lk
}
lookups <- lapply(setNames(names(BASE), names(BASE)), build_lookup)
sapply(lookups, nrow)

# every eQTL with its effect in the condition looked up in (NA = variant not tested for that gene there).
# Beta_Flu / P_Flu: the eQTL's own condition; Beta_Base / P_Base: the condition looked up in.
query_in_base <- function(comp, lk) bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(comp)), function(i) {
  b <- comp$base[i]
  signif[[comp$flu[i]]] %>% rename(Beta_Flu = Beta, P_Flu = P) %>%
    left_join(lk[[b]] %>% rename(Beta_Base = SnpWeight, P_Base = PValue), by = c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type")) %>%
    mutate(comparison = comp$comparison[i], flu = comp$flu[i], base = b,
           flu_lab = comp$flu_lab[i], base_lab = comp$base_lab[i])
})) %>%
  mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, comp$comparison), Variant_Type = factor(Variant_Type, VARIANTS),
         base_lab = factor(base_lab, unique(comp$base_lab)),
         Tested = !is.na(Beta_Base),
         Same_direction = Tested & sign(Beta_Base) == sign(Beta_Flu),
         direction = ifelse(Same_direction, "Concordant", "Discordant"),
         # direction only; significance in the condition looked up in is not used
         Category = factor(case_when(!Tested ~ "Not tested",
                                     Same_direction ~ "Same direction",
                                     TRUE ~ "Opposite direction"),
                           levels = c("Same direction", "Opposite direction", "Not tested")))
# column names for the CSV exports
export_cols <- function(d) d %>%
  transmute(comparison, condition = flu_lab, looked_up_in = base_lab, Gene, SNP, Variant_Type,
            Beta_condition = Beta_Flu, P_condition = P_Flu, Beta_looked_up_in = Beta_Base, P_looked_up_in = P_Base,
            Tested, Same_direction, Category)
flu_in_base <- query_in_base(COMP, lookups)
write.csv(export_cols(flu_in_base), file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Flu_eQTLs_in_other_conditions_all.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
conc <- flu_in_base %>% filter(Tested)
```

**Control: YPD.1 vs YPD.2.** The same lookup between the two YPD replicates (each replicate's
significant eQTLs looked up in the other), used as the reference for agreement expected from
replication alone (Section 3.1 control figure, Section 6). Cached to `replicates/`.

```{r rep-lookup}
REP_COMP <- bind_rows(make_comp(c(YPD.1 = "YPD.1"), c(YPD.1 = "YPD.1"), c(YPD.2 = "YPD.2")),
                      make_comp(c(YPD.2 = "YPD.2"), c(YPD.2 = "YPD.2"), c(YPD.1 = "YPD.1")))
REP_DIR  <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "replicates")
dir.create(REP_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)

# YPD.2 is looked up with YPD.1's eQTLs and YPD.1 with YPD.2's, so each lookup is named by the dataset it reads
rep_lookups <- list(YPD.2 = build_lookup("YPD.2", pairs = signif[["YPD.1"]] %>% distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type), out_dir = REP_DIR),
                    YPD.1 = build_lookup("YPD.1", pairs = signif[["YPD.2"]] %>% distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type), out_dir = REP_DIR))
sapply(rep_lookups, nrow)

rep_in_base <- query_in_base(REP_COMP, rep_lookups)
write.csv(export_cols(rep_in_base), file.path(REP_DIR, "YPD_replicate_eQTLs_all.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
rep_conc <- rep_in_base %>% filter(Tested)
```

# 3. Effect-size concordance

**What the numbers mean.** Each fluconazole eQTL has two signed effect sizes (beta): in the
condition it is looked up in (x) and in fluconazole (y).

- *Same direction (%)*: fraction whose beta has the same sign in both. Direction only.
- *Pearson r*: correlation of the signed betas. High r means eQTLs keep their direction **and**
  their relative strength (stronger in the other condition = stronger in fluconazole). It does not
  test whether the betas are equal: r = 1 also if every fluconazole beta is twice the other condition's beta.
- *Spearman rho*: the same on ranks, so not driven by a few large effects.
- Equal magnitude would put the points on the dashed 1:1 line, but only eQTLs significant in
  fluconazole are plotted, so their fluconazole |beta| is always large (>= ~0.4): the points sit
  above the line by selection, not biology.

Tests: one-sided binomial test of same direction > 50%; permutation tests for same direction
and Pearson r (the other condition's betas shuffled across eQTLs, `r N_PERMS` permutations, so the smallest
possible P is `r signif(1 / (N_PERMS + 1), 2)`). Binomial and Pearson P-values are
BH-adjusted within the variant-type rows and within the "All variants" rows.

```{r stats}
conc_stats <- function(d) {
  n <- nrow(d)
  if (n < 3) return(tibble(n_tested = n))
  same <- sign(d$Beta_Base) == sign(d$Beta_Flu)
  r    <- cor(d$Beta_Base, d$Beta_Flu)
  perm <- replicate(N_PERMS, { b <- sample(d$Beta_Base); c(mean(sign(b) == sign(d$Beta_Flu)), cor(b, d$Beta_Flu)) })
  tibble(n_tested = n, n_same_direction = sum(same), pct_same_direction = 100 * mean(same),
         binom_p = binom.test(sum(same), n, 0.5, alternative = "greater")$p.value,
         perm_p_same_direction = (sum(perm[1, ] >= mean(same)) + 1) / (N_PERMS + 1),
         pearson_r = r, spearman_rho = cor(d$Beta_Base, d$Beta_Flu, method = "spearman"),
         pearson_p = cor.test(d$Beta_Base, d$Beta_Flu)$p.value,
         perm_p_r = (sum(perm[2, ] >= r) + 1) / (N_PERMS + 1),
         perm_same = list(perm[1, ]), perm_r = list(perm[2, ]))
}
# per variant type, all variants, and both stacked (n_flu_eQTLs = query eQTLs in the comparison)
concordance_tables <- function(in_base, cd) {
  totals_vt  <- in_base %>% count(comparison, Variant_Type, name = "n_flu_eQTLs")
  totals_all <- in_base %>% count(comparison, name = "n_flu_eQTLs")
  vt <- cd %>% group_by(comparison, base_lab, Variant_Type) %>% group_modify(~ conc_stats(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(totals_vt, by = c("comparison", "Variant_Type")) %>%
    mutate(binom_p_BH = p.adjust(binom_p, "BH"), pearson_p_BH = p.adjust(pearson_p, "BH"))
  all <- cd %>% group_by(comparison, base_lab) %>% group_modify(~ conc_stats(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(totals_all, by = "comparison") %>% mutate(Variant_Type = "All variants") %>%
    mutate(binom_p_BH = p.adjust(binom_p, "BH"), pearson_p_BH = p.adjust(pearson_p, "BH"))
  table <- bind_rows(vt %>% mutate(Variant_Type = as.character(Variant_Type)), all) %>%
    mutate(Variant_Type = factor(Variant_Type, c(VARIANTS, "All variants")),
           pct_tested = 100 * n_tested / n_flu_eQTLs) %>%
    arrange(comparison, Variant_Type) %>%
    select(comparison, Variant_Type, n_flu_eQTLs, n_tested, pct_tested, everything(), -base_lab)
  list(vt = vt, all = all, table = table)
}
ct <- concordance_tables(flu_in_base, conc)
rep_ct <- concordance_tables(rep_in_base, rep_conc)   # YPD replicate control (Sections 3.1 and 6)
stats_vt <- ct$vt; stats_all <- ct$all; stats_table <- ct$table
write.csv(stats_table %>% select(-perm_same, -perm_r),
          file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Effect_size_concordance_by_variant_type.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(stats_table %>% select(comparison, Variant_Type, n_flu_eQTLs, n_tested, pct_same_direction,
                                    binom_p_BH, pearson_r, spearman_rho, perm_p_r),
             digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 3, 3, 3, 4))
```

## 3.1 One figure per comparison

The first figure is the control, YPD.1 eQTLs looked up in YPD.2 (two replicates of the same
condition): the agreement expected without any change of condition. All figures share the same
axis range.

All variant types in one panel. Points: eQTLs tested in the other condition, by direction.
Lines: least-squares fit per variant type (legend: n, Pearson r and % same direction per type).

```{r scatter, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, results = "asis"}
DIR_COLS <- c(Concordant = "#27AE60", Discordant = "#E74C3C")
VT_COLS  <- c(SNPs = "#3498DB", InDels = "#9B59B6", SVs = "#B7950B", CNVs = "#E67E22")
# one axis range for the control and all fluconazole figures, so they can be compared directly
lim <- max(abs(c(conc$Beta_Base, conc$Beta_Flu, rep_conc$Beta_Base, rep_conc$Beta_Flu))) * 1.05

scatter_plot <- function(i, comp = COMP, cd = conc, s_all = stats_all, s_vt = stats_vt, lim_xy = lim) {
  cm <- comp$comparison[i]
  d  <- cd %>% filter(comparison == cm)
  st <- s_all %>% filter(comparison == cm)
  vt <- s_vt %>% filter(comparison == cm)
  vt_lab <- setNames(sprintf("%s (n = %d, r = %.2f, %.0f%% same dir.)", vt$Variant_Type, vt$n_tested,
                             vt$pearson_r, vt$pct_same_direction), as.character(vt$Variant_Type))
  ggplot(d, aes(Beta_Base, Beta_Flu)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
    geom_point(aes(colour = direction), size = 1.4, alpha = 0.35) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = DIR_COLS, name = "Direction",
                        labels = c(Concordant = "Same direction", Discordant = "Opposite direction")) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
    ggnewscale::new_scale_colour() +
    geom_smooth(aes(colour = Variant_Type), method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = VT_COLS, labels = vt_lab, name = "Variant type (fit)") +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    annotate("label", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.03, vjust = 1.05, size = 4, fontface = "bold",
             label.size = 0, fill = alpha("white", 0.85),
             label = sprintf("All variants, n = %d\nSame direction = %.1f%%\nPearson r = %.2f\nSpearman rho = %.2f",
                             st$n_tested, st$pct_same_direction, st$pearson_r, st$spearman_rho)) +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(-lim_xy, lim_xy), ylim = c(-lim_xy, lim_xy)) +
    labs(title = cm,
         subtitle = sprintf("Significant %s eQTLs, effect size looked up in %s", comp$flu_lab[i], comp$base_lab[i]),
         x = bquote(bold("Effect size "*beta*", "*.(comp$base_lab[i]))),
         y = bquote(bold("Effect size "*beta*", "*.(comp$flu_lab[i])))) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 14), axis.text = element_text(size = 12, colour = "black"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
# control first: YPD.1 eQTLs looked up in YPD.2 (same condition, replicate)
i_ctrl <- which(REP_COMP$flu == "YPD.1")
cat("\n\n### ", REP_COMP$comparison[i_ctrl], " (control: YPD replicates)\n\n", sep = "")
p <- scatter_plot(i_ctrl, REP_COMP, rep_conc, rep_ct$all, rep_ct$vt, lim); print(p)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("Fig_effect_size_", REP_COMP$file_tag[i_ctrl], "_control.tiff")),
       p, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(COMP))) {
  cat("\n\n### ", COMP$comparison[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- scatter_plot(i); print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("Fig_effect_size_", COMP$file_tag[i], ".tiff")),
         p, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
```

## 3.2 Summary across variant types

```{r summary-plot, fig.width = 15, fig.height = 8}
summary_plot <- function(st_table, comp, title) {
  sum_long <- st_table %>%
    left_join(comp %>% select(comparison, flu_lab, base_lab), by = "comparison") %>%
    select(flu_lab, base_lab, Variant_Type, `Found (%)` = pct_tested,
           `Same direction (%)` = pct_same_direction, `Pearson r` = pearson_r) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(flu_lab, base_lab, Variant_Type), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(metric, c("Found (%)", "Same direction (%)", "Pearson r")),
           base_lab = factor(base_lab, unique(comp$base_lab)))
  p_sum <- ggplot(sum_long, aes(Variant_Type, value, fill = base_lab)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.85), width = 0.8, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(metric == "Pearson r", sprintf("%.2f", value), sprintf("%.0f", value))),
              position = position_dodge(0.85), vjust = -0.3, size = 2.3, fontface = "bold") +
    facet_grid(flu_lab ~ metric, scales = "free_y",
               labeller = labeller(flu_lab = function(x) paste(x, "eQTLs"))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = BASE_COLS, name = "Looked up in") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), strip.background = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 30, hjust = 1),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
  p_sum
}
p_sum <- summary_plot(stats_table, COMP, "Fluconazole eQTLs in the conditions, by variant type")
print(p_sum)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Fig_concordance_summary_by_variant_type.tiff"), p_sum,
       width = 15, height = 8, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
```

## 3.3 Permutation null distributions (all variants)

**The question.** About 80% of fluconazole eQTLs have the same direction of effect in YPD. Is that
more than we would see by chance? If most effects happened to be positive in both datasets, even
unrelated eQTLs would often "agree" in sign. The permutation test measures what chance alone gives.

**What the code does** (in `conc_stats()`, Section 3), for each comparison, e.g. fluconazole_16ug
eQTLs in YPD.1:

1. Take the real pairs: for every eQTL, its effect size (beta) in fluconazole and the effect size
   of the *same gene and same variant* in YPD.1. Compute the % with the same direction and the
   Pearson r. These are the **observed** values.
2. Shuffle the YPD.1 betas randomly across eQTLs, keeping the fluconazole betas in place. Each
   fluconazole eQTL is now paired with the YPD.1 effect of a *random other* eQTL: the values are
   real, but the link "same gene, same variant" is broken.
3. Recompute % same direction and Pearson r for the shuffled pairs.
4. Repeat 5,000 times. The 5,000 values are the **null distribution**: the agreement expected if an
   eQTL's effect in one condition had nothing to do with its effect in the other.
5. p-value = (number of shuffles with a value at least as large as the observed one + 1) / 5,001.
   If no shuffle reaches the observed value, p = 1/5,001 = 0.0002, the smallest possible.

Shuffling (instead of simply comparing with 50%) keeps each dataset's real mix of positive and
negative effects, so the chance level is estimated correctly.

**How to read the figure** (one per comparison, two panels; the sentence above each figure gives
the observed numbers):

- *Grey histogram*: the 5,000 shuffled values, i.e. what chance gives. Each bar's height (y axis)
  is how many of the 5,000 random pairings gave a value in that range of the x axis; all bars
  together add up to 5,000. For same direction it sits
  around 50%, for Pearson r around 0. It is a distribution because every shuffle is a different
  random pairing.
- *Coloured vertical line with arrow*: the value from the real data (written in the arrow label);
  only its position on the x axis matters, its height has no meaning. The real data are a single
  pairing (each eQTL with its own effect in the other condition), so they give a single value:
  the % of all compared eQTLs whose effect has the same sign in both conditions (left), or the
  Pearson r between the two conditions' effect sizes over all compared eQTLs (right). It is
  computed from *both* conditions' effect sizes, not from either alone. The individual effect
  sizes are shown in the scatter plots of Section 3.1.
- *Dashed line*: the "no agreement" reference (50% for direction, 0 for r).
- *Label*: the permutation p-value for "more than chance" (share of the 5,000 random pairings with a
  value at least as large as the observed one).

The **middle panel** is the opposite direction: the % of eQTLs whose effect has opposite signs in
the two conditions (100% minus the % same direction, in the real data and in every random pairing).
A line to the *right* of the grey histogram would mean more sign flips than chance, i.e. effects
systematically reversed between conditions. Here the line lies far to the *left* (far fewer flips
than chance), so its p-value for "more than chance" is close to 1.

**What to expect.** If effects are shared between the conditions, the coloured line lies far to
the right of the grey histogram (observed agreement much higher than any shuffle), as in every
comparison here. If effects were unrelated, the line would fall inside the histogram. A line to the
*left* of the histogram would mean fewer same-direction eQTLs than chance, i.e. systematically
reversed effects (not seen; see Section 3.5).

Note: the test treats every eQTL as independent, but eQTLs of the same gene are often linked
variants (LD), so the p-values are somewhat over-confident; the observed values are so far from the
null that this does not change the conclusion.

```{r null-plots, fig.width = 19, fig.height = 5.8, results = "asis"}
# one panel: grey histogram = statistic from 5,000 random pairings (null);
# coloured line + arrow = the same statistic from the real pairs (one value for all eQTLs of the comparison)
null_panel <- function(perm, obs, ref, col, ttl, xlab, p, pct) {
  k <- if (pct) 100 else 1
  pd <- tibble(v = perm * k); obs <- obs * k; ref <- ref * k
  expct <- mean(pd$v)
  # tallest bar: ggplot spreads the 50 bins over the whole x axis (including the observed and reference lines)
  rng  <- range(c(pd$v, obs, ref))
  ymax <- max(table(cut(pd$v, seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 51), include.lowest = TRUE)))
  obs_lab <- if (pct) sprintf("%.1f%%", obs) else sprintf("r = %.2f", obs)
  x_txt <- expct + 0.55 * (obs - expct)
  ggplot(pd, aes(v)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(fill = "Random pairings (5,000 permutations)"), bins = 50, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = obs, colour = col, linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +
    annotate("text", x = expct, y = ymax * 1.08, label = "chance", size = 3.5, colour = "grey35", fontface = "italic") +
    annotate("segment", x = x_txt, xend = obs, y = ymax * 0.45, yend = ymax * 0.3, colour = col, linewidth = 0.8,
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
    annotate("label", x = x_txt, y = ymax * 0.45, label = paste0("Observed (real data)\n", obs_lab), size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
             colour = col, label.size = 0, fill = alpha("white", 0.85)) +
    annotate("label", x = (expct + obs) / 2, y = Inf, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1.1, size = 3.2, label.size = 0, fill = alpha("white", 0.85),
             label = paste("permutation p (more than chance) =", if (p < 0.001) sprintf("%.1e", p) else sprintf("%.3f", p))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Random pairings (5,000 permutations)" = "grey70"), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    labs(title = ttl, x = xlab, y = "Number of random pairings (out of 5,000)") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
          legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
}
null_plot <- function(st) {
  # printed summary of the observed data above each figure
  cat(sprintf(paste0("\n\nOf %s eQTLs compared (same gene, same variant), %s (%.1f%%) have the same direction of effect in both ",
                     "conditions and %s (%.1f%%) the opposite direction. Random pairing of eQTLs gives on average %.1f%% same ",
                     "direction and %.1f%% opposite direction. Pearson r of the effect sizes: %.2f observed, %.2f on average ",
                     "for random pairing.\n\n"),
              format(st$n_tested, big.mark = ","), format(st$n_same_direction, big.mark = ","), st$pct_same_direction,
              format(st$n_tested - st$n_same_direction, big.mark = ","), 100 - st$pct_same_direction,
              100 * mean(st$perm_same[[1]]), 100 - 100 * mean(st$perm_same[[1]]),
              st$pearson_r, {m <- mean(st$perm_r[[1]]); if (abs(m) < 0.005) 0 else m}))
  # opposite direction = 1 - same direction, in the real data and in every permutation;
  # p: share of permutations with at least as many opposite-direction eQTLs as observed
  p_opp <- (sum(st$perm_same[[1]] <= st$pct_same_direction / 100) + 1) / (length(st$perm_same[[1]]) + 1)
  (null_panel(st$perm_same[[1]], st$pct_same_direction / 100, 0.5, "#1B7837", "Same direction of effect",
              "% of eQTLs with the same sign of effect in both conditions", st$perm_p_same_direction, pct = TRUE) |
   null_panel(1 - st$perm_same[[1]], 1 - st$pct_same_direction / 100, 0.5, "#B2182B", "Opposite direction of effect",
              "% of eQTLs with the opposite sign of effect in the two conditions", p_opp, pct = TRUE) |
   null_panel(st$perm_r[[1]], st$pearson_r, 0, "#2C7FB8", "Correlation of effect sizes",
              "Pearson r", st$perm_p_r, pct = FALSE)) +
    plot_annotation(title = as.character(st$comparison),
                    subtitle = "Grey: 5,000 random pairings of eQTLs (chance). Coloured line: the value from the real data.",
                    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
                                  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey30")))
}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(COMP))) {
  cat("\n\n### ", COMP$comparison[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- null_plot(stats_all %>% filter(comparison == COMP$comparison[i])); print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("Fig_null_distribution_", COMP$file_tag[i], ".tiff")),
         p, width = 19, height = 5.8, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
```

## 3.4 eQTLs significant in both conditions

The comparisons above use every fluconazole eQTL found (tested) in the other condition, whatever
its p-value there. Here only the gene-variant pairs that are **significant in both conditions**
are kept, i.e. eQTLs detected independently in each. For these, the same statistics are reported,
next to the values for all found eQTLs. First row: the control (YPD.1 eQTLs in YPD.2, two
replicates of the same condition). `ratio_same_dir` = median |beta in the other condition| /
|beta in the eQTL's own condition| over same-direction eQTLs (1 = same magnitude);
`spearman_abs_beta` = Spearman correlation of the magnitudes |beta| only.

```{r sig-both, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 10}
ctrl_comp <- REP_COMP$comparison[REP_COMP$flu == "YPD.1"]
found_all <- bind_rows(rep_conc %>% filter(comparison == ctrl_comp), conc) %>%
  mutate(comparison = factor(as.character(comparison), c(ctrl_comp, COMP$comparison)))

# keep pairs that are also significant in the condition looked up in
sig_both <- bind_rows(lapply(split(found_all, found_all$base), function(x)
  semi_join(x, signif[[x$base[1]]], by = c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type"))))

eff_stats <- function(d) d %>% group_by(comparison) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct_same_direction = 100 * mean(Same_direction),
            pearson_r = if (n() > 2) cor(Beta_Flu, Beta_Base) else NA_real_,
            spearman_rho = if (n() > 2) cor(Beta_Flu, Beta_Base, method = "spearman") else NA_real_,
            spearman_abs_beta = if (n() > 2) cor(abs(Beta_Flu), abs(Beta_Base), method = "spearman") else NA_real_,
            ratio_same_dir = median(abs(Beta_Base[Same_direction]) / abs(Beta_Flu[Same_direction])),
            .groups = "drop")
sig_tab <- full_join(eff_stats(sig_both), eff_stats(found_all), by = "comparison", suffix = c("_sig_both", "_all_found")) %>%
  arrange(comparison)
write.csv(sig_tab, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Effect_size_sig_in_both_vs_all_found.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(sig_tab %>% select(comparison, n_sig_both, pct_same_direction_sig_both, pearson_r_sig_both,
                                spearman_rho_sig_both, spearman_abs_beta_sig_both, ratio_same_dir_sig_both,
                                n_all_found, pct_same_direction_all_found, pearson_r_all_found,
                                spearman_abs_beta_all_found, ratio_same_dir_all_found),
             digits = 2, caption = "eQTLs significant in both conditions vs all found eQTLs (first row: control)")

lab_sig <- sig_tab %>% transmute(comparison, label = sprintf("n = %d\nsame dir. = %.0f%%\nr = %.2f",
                                                           n_sig_both, pct_same_direction_sig_both, pearson_r_sig_both))
lim_sig <- max(abs(c(sig_both$Beta_Base, sig_both$Beta_Flu))) * 1.05
p <- ggplot(sig_both, aes(Beta_Base, Beta_Flu)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = direction), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_label(data = lab_sig, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label), hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.1,
             size = 3, label.size = 0, fill = alpha("white", 0.8), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = DIR_COLS, labels = c(Concordant = "Same direction", Discordant = "Opposite direction"),
                      name = "Direction", drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison, ncol = 4, labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-lim_sig, lim_sig), ylim = c(-lim_sig, lim_sig)) +
  labs(title = "eQTLs significant in both conditions (same gene, same variant)",
       x = expression(bold("Effect size " * beta * ", condition looked up in")),
       y = expression(bold("Effect size " * beta * ", eQTL's own condition"))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Fig_effect_size_sig_in_both.tiff"), p, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 600,
       compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
```

## 3.5 Same or opposite direction: more than chance?

Two questions, each against what chance alone would give (first row: the control).

**Whole set (permutation null of Section 3.3).** Shuffling the other condition's betas across
eQTLs gives the % same direction expected if an eQTL's effect in one condition were unrelated to
its effect in the other (`expected_pct_same`; % opposite = 100 - % same). `p_same_above_chance`:
are there more same-direction eQTLs than chance? `p_opposite_above_chance`: are there more
opposite-direction eQTLs than chance (expected if effects were systematically reversed)?

**Per eQTL (p-value in the other condition).** If a fluconazole eQTL has *no* effect in the other
condition, its p-value there is random (uniform: ~5% below 0.05, flat histogram) and its
direction is a coin flip. If its effect is *reversed* there, opposite-direction eQTLs would show
an excess of small p-values. `pct_p05` is the % of eQTLs with p < 0.05 in the other condition
(5% expected by chance), with a one-sided binomial test against 5%. In the histograms the dashed
line is the chance (uniform) expectation.

```{r direction-chance, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 10}
perm_all <- bind_rows(rep_ct$all %>% filter(comparison == ctrl_comp), stats_all) %>%
  mutate(comparison = factor(as.character(comparison), levels(found_all$comparison)))
chance_tab <- perm_all %>% rowwise() %>%
  transmute(comparison, n_found = n_tested,
            observed_pct_same = pct_same_direction, expected_pct_same = 100 * mean(perm_same),
            p_same_above_chance = perm_p_same_direction,
            observed_pct_opposite = 100 - pct_same_direction, expected_pct_opposite = 100 - 100 * mean(perm_same),
            p_opposite_above_chance = (sum(perm_same <= pct_same_direction / 100) + 1) / (N_PERMS + 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% arrange(comparison)
write.csv(chance_tab, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Direction_vs_chance_permutation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(chance_tab, digits = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 4, 1, 1, 4),
             caption = "Observed vs chance (permutation) % same and % opposite direction")

pval_tab <- found_all %>%
  mutate(direction = ifelse(Same_direction, "Same direction", "Opposite direction")) %>%
  group_by(comparison, direction) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct_p05 = 100 * mean(P_Base < 0.05), median_p = median(P_Base),
            binom_p_vs_5pct = binom.test(sum(P_Base < 0.05), n(), 0.05, alternative = "greater")$p.value,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(comparison, desc(direction))
write.csv(pval_tab, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Direction_pvalue_in_other_condition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(pval_tab, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4),
             caption = "p-value in the other condition, by direction (chance: 5% below 0.05, median 0.5)")
cat("\n")

p <- found_all %>%
  mutate(direction = factor(ifelse(Same_direction, "Same direction", "Opposite direction"),
                            c("Same direction", "Opposite direction"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(P_Base, fill = direction)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.05), position = "identity",
                 alpha = 0.55, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Same direction" = "#1B7837", "Opposite direction" = "#B2182B"), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison, ncol = 4, labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
  labs(title = "p-value in the condition looked up in, by direction of effect",
       subtitle = "Dashed line: expected if the eQTL had no effect there (uniform p-values)",
       x = "p-value in the condition looked up in", y = "Density") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
        legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Fig_direction_pvalue_in_other_condition.tiff"), p, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 600,
       compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
```

The same result as one bar per comparison and direction: the % of eQTLs with p < 0.05 in the
condition looked up in. The dashed line is the 5% expected by chance (eQTL with no effect there).
Bars far above the line: real shared effects. Bars at or below the line: no detectable effect, so
the direction is a coin flip.

```{r direction-chance-bars, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7}
p <- pval_tab %>%
  # reversed levels so that, after coord_flip, same direction is drawn above opposite direction
  mutate(direction = factor(direction, c("Opposite direction", "Same direction")),
         comparison = factor(comparison, rev(levels(found_all$comparison)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(comparison, pct_p05, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_p05)), position = position_dodge(0.8), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 5, linetype = "Expected by chance (5%)")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Same direction" = "#1B7837", "Opposite direction" = "#B2182B"),
                    breaks = c("Same direction", "Opposite direction"), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Expected by chance (5%)" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "eQTLs with p < 0.05 in the condition looked up in",
       subtitle = "Same-direction eQTLs: far above chance (shared effects). Opposite-direction eQTLs: at or below chance (noise).",
       x = NULL, y = "% of eQTLs with p < 0.05 in the condition looked up in") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey30", size = 10),
        legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"))
print(p)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Fig_direction_pct_p05_vs_chance.tiff"), p, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 600,
       compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
```

# 4. Are fluconazole eQTLs seen in the other conditions?

Every significant fluconazole eQTL falls in one category per comparison, based only on the
direction of its effect: the same variant-gene pair is tested in the other condition with the **same**
direction of effect, tested with the **opposite** direction, or **not tested** there (variant not
in that condition's FaST-LMM output for that gene, so no effect size to compare). Whether the eQTL
is also significant in the other condition is not used.

```{r sharing, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 7}
share_table <- function(in_base) in_base %>% count(flu_lab, base_lab, Variant_Type, Category, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  bind_rows(in_base %>% count(flu_lab, base_lab, Category, .drop = FALSE) %>% mutate(Variant_Type = "All variants")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(flu_lab)) %>%
  group_by(flu_lab, base_lab, Variant_Type) %>% mutate(Pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Variant_Type = factor(Variant_Type, c(VARIANTS, "All variants")))
share <- share_table(flu_in_base)
write.csv(share, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Flu_eQTL_categories_in_other_conditions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

CAT_COLS <- c("Same direction" = "#1B7837", "Opposite direction" = "#B2182B",
              "Not tested" = "grey70")
# `what` = the query condition, as it should read in axis labels and titles
share_plot <- function(sh, what) sh %>% filter(Variant_Type == "All variants") %>%
  ggplot(aes(base_lab, Pct, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(Pct >= 4, sprintf("%.0f%%", Pct), "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  facet_wrap(~ flu_lab, labeller = labeller(flu_lab = function(x) paste(x, "eQTLs"))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = CAT_COLS, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
  labs(x = "Looked up in", y = paste0("% of ", what, " eQTLs"),
       title = paste0(str_to_sentence(what), " eQTLs in other conditions")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13), strip.background = element_blank())
p_share <- share_plot(share, "fluconazole")
print(p_share)
```

# 5. Galactose eQTLs in other conditions

Sections 2-4 repeated for galactose (scgal.1): each significant galactose eQTL is looked up in
YPD.1, YPD.2, synthetic complete, YPD (integrated), synthetic complete (integrated), fluconazole_16ug
and fluconazole_8ug. The other dataset is on x, galactose on y.
Outputs (same file names as for
fluconazole, with `scgal_1` in place of `Flu_16ug`) go to `galactose/`.

```{r gal-lookup}
GAL      <- c(scgal.1 = "galactose")
GAL_BASE <- c(BASE, Flu.1 = "fluconazole_16ug", Flu.2 = "fluconazole_8ug")   # same five conditions + both doses
GAL_COMP <- make_comp(GAL, GAL, GAL_BASE)
GAL_DIR  <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "galactose")
dir.create(GAL_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)

gal_pairs   <- signif[["scgal.1"]] %>% distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type)
gal_lookups <- lapply(setNames(names(GAL_BASE), names(GAL_BASE)), build_lookup, pairs = gal_pairs, out_dir = GAL_DIR)
sapply(gal_lookups, nrow)

gal_in_base <- query_in_base(GAL_COMP, gal_lookups)
write.csv(export_cols(gal_in_base), file.path(GAL_DIR, "Gal_eQTLs_in_other_conditions_all.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
gal_conc <- gal_in_base %>% filter(Tested)
```

## 5.1 Effect-size concordance

```{r gal-stats}
gal_ct <- concordance_tables(gal_in_base, gal_conc)
write.csv(gal_ct$table %>% select(-perm_same, -perm_r) %>% rename(n_gal_eQTLs = n_flu_eQTLs),
          file.path(GAL_DIR, "Effect_size_concordance_by_variant_type.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(gal_ct$table %>% select(comparison, Variant_Type, n_gal_eQTLs = n_flu_eQTLs, n_tested,
                                     pct_same_direction, binom_p_BH, pearson_r, spearman_rho, perm_p_r),
             digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 3, 3, 3, 4))
```

```{r gal-scatter, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, results = "asis"}
gal_lim <- max(abs(c(gal_conc$Beta_Base, gal_conc$Beta_Flu))) * 1.05
for (i in seq_len(nrow(GAL_COMP))) {
  cat("\n\n### ", GAL_COMP$comparison[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- scatter_plot(i, GAL_COMP, gal_conc, gal_ct$all, gal_ct$vt, gal_lim); print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(GAL_DIR, paste0("Fig_effect_size_", GAL_COMP$file_tag[i], ".tiff")),
         p, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
```

```{r gal-summary-plot, fig.width = 15, fig.height = 5}
p <- summary_plot(gal_ct$table, GAL_COMP, "Galactose eQTLs in the conditions, by variant type")
print(p)
ggsave(file.path(GAL_DIR, "Fig_concordance_summary_by_variant_type.tiff"), p,
       width = 15, height = 5, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
```

```{r gal-null-plots, fig.width = 19, fig.height = 5.8, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(GAL_COMP))) {
  cat("\n\n### ", GAL_COMP$comparison[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- null_plot(gal_ct$all %>% filter(comparison == GAL_COMP$comparison[i])); print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(GAL_DIR, paste0("Fig_null_distribution_", GAL_COMP$file_tag[i], ".tiff")),
         p, width = 19, height = 5.8, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
```

# 6. Replicate reference: YPD.1 vs YPD.2

The same same-gene, same-variant comparison between the two YPD replicates, in both directions:
each significant YPD.1 eQTL is looked up among all tested variants of YPD.2, and each significant
YPD.2 eQTL in YPD.1. The condition is identical, so this is the agreement expected from
replication alone (noise, and effects inflated in the dataset the eQTL was found in). Differences
between conditions (Sections 3 and 5) are only meaningful relative to this reference. The lookup is
done in Section 2; outputs go to `replicates/`.


```{r rep-stats}
write.csv(rep_ct$table %>% select(-perm_same, -perm_r) %>% rename(n_eQTLs = n_flu_eQTLs),
          file.path(REP_DIR, "Effect_size_concordance_by_variant_type.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(rep_ct$table %>% select(comparison, Variant_Type, n_eQTLs = n_flu_eQTLs, n_tested,
                                     pct_same_direction, binom_p_BH, pearson_r, spearman_rho, perm_p_r),
             digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 3, 3, 3, 4))
```

```{r rep-scatter, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, results = "asis"}
rep_lim <- max(abs(c(rep_conc$Beta_Base, rep_conc$Beta_Flu))) * 1.05
for (i in seq_len(nrow(REP_COMP))) {
  cat("\n\n### ", REP_COMP$comparison[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- scatter_plot(i, REP_COMP, rep_conc, rep_ct$all, rep_ct$vt, rep_lim); print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(REP_DIR, paste0("Fig_effect_size_", REP_COMP$file_tag[i], ".tiff")),
         p, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
```

```{r rep-summary-plot, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7}

print(p)
ggsave(file.path(REP_DIR, "Fig_concordance_summary_by_variant_type.tiff"), p,
       width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
```

```{r rep-null-plots, fig.width = 19, fig.height = 5.8, results = "asis"}

  cat("\n\n### ", REP_COMP$comparison[i], "\n\n", sep = "")

  ggsave(file.path(REP_DIR, paste0("Fig_null_distribution_", REP_COMP$file_tag[i], ".tiff")),
```

# 7. All comparisons side by side (all variant types pooled)

Each condition's significant eQTLs, same gene and same variant looked up in the other condition.
`ratio_same_dir` is the median |beta in the other condition| / |beta in the eQTL's own condition|
over the same-direction eQTLs (1 = same magnitude); compare each value with the YPD replicate rows.

```{r all-comparisons}
ratio_tbl <- bind_rows(conc, gal_conc, rep_conc) %>% filter(Same_direction) %>%
  group_by(comparison) %>% summarise(ratio_same_dir = median(abs(Beta_Base) / abs(Beta_Flu)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(comparison = as.character(comparison))
all_comp <- bind_rows(rep_ct$all %>% mutate(set = "YPD replicates (reference)"),
                      stats_all %>% mutate(set = "Fluconazole"),
                      gal_ct$all %>% mutate(set = "Galactose")) %>%
  mutate(comparison = as.character(comparison)) %>%
  left_join(ratio_tbl, by = "comparison") %>%
  transmute(set, comparison, n_eQTLs = n_flu_eQTLs, n_tested,
            n_same_direction, n_opposite_direction = n_tested - n_same_direction,
            pct_same_direction, pearson_r, spearman_rho, ratio_same_dir, binom_p_BH)
write.csv(all_comp, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Effect_size_concordance_all_comparisons.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(all_comp, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3),
             caption = "Same-gene, same-variant effect-size comparison, all variant types pooled")
```

# 8. Summary: eQTLs found in the other condition

Per comparison (e.g. "fluconazole_16ug eQTLs in YPD.1"), starting from the significant eQTLs of one
condition (fluconazole_16ug) and looking up the same gene and same variant among *all tested*
associations of the other condition (YPD.1; any p-value, significance there is not used). Comparisons follow
the design above: each dataset against a *different* condition; the only same-condition pair is
YPD.1 vs YPD.2 (replicate reference); integrated datasets are never compared with their own
replicates.

- *Found in the other condition*: the same gene-variant pair is tested there, so its effect size
  can be compared. *Not found*: not tested there.
- *Same / opposite direction*: sign of the effect in the other condition vs the eQTL's own
  condition, for found eQTLs.
- *Genes*: genes with at least one significant eQTL, and genes with at least one such eQTL found in
  the other condition (split into genes whose found eQTLs all keep their direction, all
  change direction, or both), as counts and as % of genes expressed in both datasets
  (genes in both `gene_matrix.txt` files).

```{r overlap-summary, results = "asis"}
# genes expressed (tested) in each dataset = rows of its phenotype matrix (expression-filtered genes used in the GWAS)
PHENO <- c(Flu.1 = "Flu.1/fastlmm", Flu.2 = "Flu.2/fastlmm", YPD.1 = "YPD.1/fastlmm", YPD.2 = "YPD.2/fastlmm",
           sc2glu.2 = "sc2glu.2/fastlmm_sc2.glu.2_only", YPD_integrated = "merged_YPD/fastlmm",
           sc2glu_integrated = "sc2glu.2/fastlmm", scgal.1 = "scgal.1/fastlmm")
tested_genes <- lapply(PHENO, function(d)
  fread(file.path(ROOT, d, "data/pheno_data/gene_matrix.txt"), select = 1)[[1]])

overlap_summary <- function(comp, in_base) bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(comp)), function(i) {
  cm <- comp$comparison[i]; q <- comp$flu[i]; b <- comp$base[i]
  expressed <- intersect(tested_genes[[q]], tested_genes[[b]])
  d     <- in_base %>% filter(comparison == cm)
  found <- d %>% filter(Tested)
  g_dir <- found %>% group_by(Gene) %>% summarise(same = all(Same_direction), opp = all(!Same_direction), .groups = "drop")
  pct_e <- function(g) 100 * length(intersect(g, expressed)) / length(expressed)
  tibble(comparison = cm, condition1 = comp$flu_lab[i], condition2 = comp$base_lab[i],
         eQTLs_condition1 = nrow(d),
         eQTLs_found = nrow(found), pct_found = 100 * nrow(found) / nrow(d),
         eQTLs_not_found = nrow(d) - nrow(found),
         eQTLs_same_direction = sum(found$Same_direction), pct_same_direction = 100 * mean(found$Same_direction),
         eQTLs_opposite_direction = sum(!found$Same_direction), pct_opposite_direction = 100 * mean(!found$Same_direction),
         genes_expressed_both = length(expressed),
         genes_condition1 = n_distinct(d$Gene), pct_genes_condition1 = pct_e(unique(d$Gene)),
         genes_found = nrow(g_dir), pct_genes_found = pct_e(g_dir$Gene),
         genes_all_same_direction = sum(g_dir$same), genes_all_opposite_direction = sum(g_dir$opp),
         genes_mixed_direction = sum(!g_dir$same & !g_dir$opp))
}))
overlap <- bind_rows(overlap_summary(REP_COMP, rep_in_base) %>% mutate(set = "YPD replicates (reference)"),
                     overlap_summary(COMP, flu_in_base) %>% mutate(set = "Fluconazole"),
                     overlap_summary(GAL_COMP, gal_in_base) %>% mutate(set = "Galactose")) %>% relocate(set)

write.csv(overlap %>% rename(condition = condition1, looked_up_in = condition2, eQTLs = eQTLs_condition1,
                             genes_with_eQTL = genes_condition1, pct_genes_with_eQTL = pct_genes_condition1),
          file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "eQTLs_found_in_other_condition_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# one readable paragraph per comparison
for (k in seq_len(nrow(overlap))) with(overlap[k, ], cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "**%s.** Of %d significant %s eQTLs, %d (%.1f%%) are found (same gene, same variant) among the tested associations of %s ",
  "and %d are not tested there. Of the found eQTLs, %d (%.1f%%) have the same direction of effect and %d (%.1f%%) the opposite direction. ",
  "Of %d genes expressed in both datasets, %d (%.1f%%) have a significant %s eQTL and %d (%.1f%%) have at least one such eQTL found in %s: ",
  "%d with all found eQTLs in the same direction, %d with all in the opposite direction and %d with both.\n\n"),
  comparison, eQTLs_condition1, condition1, eQTLs_found, pct_found, condition2, eQTLs_not_found,
  eQTLs_same_direction, pct_same_direction, eQTLs_opposite_direction, pct_opposite_direction,
  genes_expressed_both, genes_condition1, pct_genes_condition1, condition1, genes_found, pct_genes_found, condition2,
  genes_all_same_direction, genes_all_opposite_direction, genes_mixed_direction)))

# transposed tables: one row per measure, one column per comparison, one table per set
n_pct <- function(n, p) sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(n, big.mark = ","), p)
fmt_n <- function(n) format(n, big.mark = ",")
summary_wide <- overlap %>%
  transmute(set, column = comparison,
            `Significant eQTLs`                                      = fmt_n(eQTLs_condition1),
            `Found in the other condition (% of eQTLs)`             = n_pct(eQTLs_found, pct_found),
            `Not found in the other condition`                       = fmt_n(eQTLs_not_found),
            `Same direction (% of found)`                           = n_pct(eQTLs_same_direction, pct_same_direction),
            `Opposite direction (% of found)`                       = n_pct(eQTLs_opposite_direction, pct_opposite_direction),
            `Genes expressed in both datasets`                      = fmt_n(genes_expressed_both),
            `Genes with a significant eQTL (% expressed)`           = n_pct(genes_condition1, pct_genes_condition1),
            `Genes with an eQTL found in the other condition (% expressed)` = n_pct(genes_found, pct_genes_found),
            `Genes: all found eQTLs same direction`                 = fmt_n(genes_all_same_direction),
            `Genes: all found eQTLs opposite direction`             = fmt_n(genes_all_opposite_direction),
            `Genes: mixed direction`                                = fmt_n(genes_mixed_direction))
measures <- setdiff(names(summary_wide), c("set", "column"))
for (st in unique(summary_wide$set)) {
  w <- summary_wide %>% filter(set == st) %>% select(-set)
  tw <- tibble(Measure = measures)
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(w))) tw[[w$column[k]]] <- unlist(w[k, measures])
  write.csv(tw, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("Summary_table_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", st), ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(tw, caption = paste0(st, ": eQTLs found in the other condition (same gene, same variant), by direction")))
}
```
